name: Milawa
bio_draft: Small village in the King Valley with cellar doors and a gourmet food stop.

facts.claim: Milawa is a village and the northern end of the King Valley, at 155 m altitude
It is the centre of the Milawa Gourmet Region, Australia's first official gourmet region, with Oxley, Tarrawingee, Markwood and Whorouly
Brown Brothers Cellar Door and Milawa Cheese Company are its best-known stops
Wangaratta to Milawa section of the Murray to Mountains Rail Trail is a 5 km ride

name: King Valley
bio_draft: Wine and food valley around Whitfield, Cheshunt and Milawa, known for prosecco.

facts.claim: Wine and agricultural region centred on the King River between Wangaratta and the Alpine National Park
Italian migrants of the 1940s-50s moved from tobacco to wine, producing sangiovese, nebbiolo and barbera
Some of Australia's highest vineyards, about 800 m, are on the Whitlands Plateau
The former Whitfield railway line route is now a rail trail

name: Warby-Ovens National Park
bio_draft: National park of the Warby Ranges near Wangaratta, with bushwalks.

facts.claim: Park about 10 km from Wangaratta protecting river red gum forest on the Ovens River, box-ironbark forest and the granite Warby Range
Ryan's Lookout and Kwat Kwat Lookout give exceptional views, with snow-covered peaks visible in winter
Spring wildflowers in the Warby Range; walking, cycling, canoeing and camping

Ticket also includes Kellyland's museum with the Railway Tavern bar, wanted posters, Ned's death mask and John Dollery paintings

name: Tallangatta
bio_draft: Town on the shore of Lake Hume, with the relocated old town nearby.

facts.claim: Town on the Mitta Arm of Lake Hume, about 38 km south-east of Albury-Wodonga
The town was moved 8 km west in the 1950s to Bolga to make way for Lake Hume's expansion
The entry sign reads 'the town that moved in the 1950s'

name: Paradise Falls (Cheshunt)
bio_draft: Waterfall in Alpine National Park, 31 m high and reached by a viewing platform.

facts.claim: Paradise Falls is a waterfall in Alpine National Park, about 20 minutes from Whitfield.
It is reached by a short 500 m walk and is best after rain.

name: Lake William Hovell
bio_draft: Lake near Cheshunt with swimming, paddling and picnic areas.

facts.claim: Lake William Hovell is a reservoir at the top of the King River valley, about 18 km from Cheshunt.
Visitors picnic and barbecue on the foreshore, fish, canoe and walk the shoreline.
It has a designated swimming area, and jet-skis and water-skiing are not allowed.

access_note: No camping or fires at the lake (per authority brochure).

name: Dartmouth Dam
bio_draft: Large dam on the Mitta Mitta River with a lookout and boating.

facts.claim: Dartmouth Dam is a 180 m high dam across the Mitta Mitta River in north-east Victoria, near Mount Bogong.
It is operated by Goulburn-Murray Water for the Murray-Darling Basin Authority and has a grassed picnic area, boat ramp, playground, fishing and camping.
It is the largest-capacity dam in Victoria.

name: Australian Alps Walking Track
bio_draft: Long-distance walking track linking the Australian Alps, with sections through the High Country.

facts.claim: The track runs about 650 km from Walhalla in Victoria to Tharwa near Canberra.
It follows ridges and high plains through Baw Baw, Alpine, Kosciuszko and Namadgi national parks and mostly avoids towns.
Many walkers do shorter sections such as the Baw Baw Plateau and the Bogong High Plains.

access_note: Remote, multi-week; current track conditions published on the agency page. Pin is a Victorian section, not route midpoint.

name: Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail
bio_draft: Rail trail for cycling and walking from Wodonga to Bright and Wangaratta.

facts.claim: A sealed off-road cycling and walking trail from Wangaratta to Bright, with a branch to Beechworth.
The main route is about 95 km; a separate section links Rutherglen to Wahgunyah on the Murray.
It follows the route of the former Bright railway line.

name: Omeo
bio_draft: Historic high country town on the Omeo Highway, a gateway to the southern Victorian Alps.

facts.claim: Omeo is a small town on the Great Alpine Road east of Mount Hotham, known as the City of the Alps.
Gold was found in Livingstone Creek in 1845 and many historic buildings remain.
Attractions include the Justice Precinct with its 1893 court house and the Oriental Claims gold diggings.

name: Omeo Mountain Bike Park
bio_draft: Mountain biking park with over 114 km of trails near Omeo.

facts.claim: A 114 km network of gravity and cross-country mountain bike trails officially opened on 5 December 2025.
Trails range from family-friendly green trails along Livingstone Creek to double-black gravity descents with up to 590 m of vertical drop.
Trails run through Sam Hill State Forest and Mt Mesley and converge at Livingstone Park, with an asphalt pump track at the trailhead.

access_note: Riding the trails appears free; uplift shuttles are separate paid extras (Blue Dirt 1-day pass from about AUD 95).

name: Corryong
bio_draft: Upper Murray town on the Snowy River, the setting of Banjo Paterson's poem The Man from Snowy River.

facts.claim: Upper Murray town in north-east Victoria, promoted as the setting of The Man from Snowy River.
Corryong cemetery holds the grave of Jack Riley (1841-1914), the stockman linked to the poem's hero.
The town hosts The Man from Snowy River Bush Festival each April (event, not a spot).

bio_draft: State park around Mount Lawson with a summit loop nature trail.

facts.claim: State park about 70 km east of Albury-Wodonga, between the Murray Valley Highway and the Murray River.
Short and medium-length walking tracks lead to lookouts, waterfalls and rocky creeks.
Mt Lawson Road gives unsealed, fine-weather two-wheel-drive access to most visitor areas.

name: Flinders Street Station
bio_draft: historic railway station at the heart of the city, with its famous front steps and clock-face facade.

facts.claim: Busiest railway station in Victoria, at Flinders and Swanston streets opposite Federation Square.
The current Federation/Edwardian Baroque building was completed in 1909 to a design by James W. Fawcett.
The 1854 station was the terminus of the first railway in Australia.

facts.claim: Opened in 1878; covers over seven hectares and is billed the largest open-air market in the Southern Hemisphere.
Victorian Heritage Register and National Heritage List site, with an estimated ten million visitors a year.
Official site lists Night Market, tours and Queen's Food Hall.

name: NGV International
bio_draft: the National Gallery of Victoria's international art collection on St Kilda Road.

facts.claim: NGV International is at 180 St Kilda Road, Melbourne
Its collection spans art from Europe, Asia, America and Oceania
General entry is free; some special exhibitions are ticketed

name: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria
bio_draft: one of the world's finest botanic gardens, 38 hectares of lakes and plantings, free to enter.

facts.claim: Melbourne Gardens covers 38 hectares and was founded in 1846 on the south side of the Yarra
The gardens slope to the river with lakes, lawns and almost 50,000 plants of 8,500 taxa
Entry is free; guided walks and the Explorer minibus are bookable

The Australian Sports Museum is housed at the ground

The first Parliament of Australia opened here on 9 May 1901
The Dome Promenade reopened to public tours in October 2022; adult tour $29
